name: Input
summary: Collects a single line of free-form text.
description: A single-line field for text the user types themselves, like a name, an email address, or a search query. It always needs a visible label, and the error state is what most changes how you use it: reserve room for the message so the layout doesn't jump.
whenToUse: The answer is short, open-ended text that you can't offer as a list of choices.
The user is searching or filtering and needs to type freely.
whenNotToUse: The answer comes from a fixed set of options. Use Select for many choices or Radio for a few.
The answer runs to several lines, like a comment or a description. Use Textarea.

size.md: The default size for most forms.

states.default: At rest and ready to accept typing.
states.focus: The field has keyboard focus and shows a focus ring.
states.error: What the user typed didn't pass validation, and the message says why.
states.disabled: Can't be typed in or tabbed to.

dos: Pair every field with a visible label.
Put format hints in helper text.
Reserve space for the error message.
donts: Don't use the placeholder as the only label. Add a real label.
Don't validate on every keystroke before the first blur.

keyboard: Tab moves focus to and from the field.
notes: Give every field a label element that points at it. A placeholder disappears as soon as the user types, so it can't do this job.
In the error state, set aria-invalid and link the message with aria-describedby so screen readers announce it.
Mark a decorative leading icon aria-hidden so it isn't announced.
